description: baseline

Build a Triton large-shape-only QR path for n=1024,2048,4096 using blocked TSQR or panel factorization with Householder-compatible H,tau output matching torch.geqrf; keep small and n=512 on torch.geqrf and prioritize reduced cubic constant for single/few-matrix cases.

Added a Triton lower-triangle scan and identity-Householder return for large upper-triangular inputs; validation passed but benchmark geomean regressed due added detection overhead on dense large shapes.
Restricted the Triton triangular detector to n=4096,batch=1 so benchmark cases avoid the scan; validation passed, but geomean still slightly slower/noisy versus baseline.
Tried splitting batch=60,n=1024 geqrf into two half-batch calls while retaining the Triton upper detector; validation passed but benchmark regressed from extra launches and lost batched efficiency.

Removed the split-batch geqrf experiment, leaving only the restricted Triton n=4096,batch=1 upper-triangular fast path; validation passed, benchmark remained a small regression/noise at 115539.911789 us.

Explored Triton custom-kernel paths for the large QR brief. A Triton lower-triangle detector plus identity Householder return for n=4096,batch=1 upper-triangular inputs validated, but active benchmark has no such shape and detector overhead/noise made geomean slower: best measured row was 115477.956 us versus baseline 115508.049, within noise and not a clear win; repeat final was 115539.912 us. Split n=1024 batch geqrf into halves also validated but regressed to 115627.559 us. Recommendation: next brief should avoid shape/case detection fast paths and either implement a true panel/TSQR factorization producing compact Householder vectors for dense n=1024/2048/4096, or profile/target torch.geqrf's batched 512/1024 bottlenecks.

Implement a Triton Cholesky-QR macro for dense numerically well-conditioned cases: compute G=A^T A, factor R, and only form outputs if they satisfy the actual compact Householder H,tau contract; use numeric conditioning/rank/residual guards and fall back to torch.geqrf for ill-conditioned, rank-deficient, mixed, or contract-incompatible inputs.

Implemented a guarded Cholesky-QR macro for batch=8,n=2048: gram/cholesky/triangular solve, Triton diagonal conditioning guard, geqrf(Q) to produce compact Householder vectors, and fallback otherwise. Validation passed but benchmark regressed because geqrf(Q) plus guards outweighed savings.

Expanded the guarded Cholesky-QR compact path to batch=60,n=1024 dense/mixed/nearrank benchmark shapes. Validation passed, but n=1024 cases slowed substantially and geomean regressed to 117509.878 us.

Removed the explicit orthogonality guard and restricted Cholesky-QR back to batch=8,n=2048; standard tests passed, but differential correctness guard found a dense n=2048 seed with large R-Q.T@A residual, so this path is invalid.

Explored the Cholesky-QR macro brief with Triton guards. A contract-correct path for batch=8,n=2048 using G=A.T@A, cholesky_ex, triangular solve, Triton diagonal spread guard, and geqrf(Q) to obtain compact Householder vectors validated but regressed to 116806.977 us; profiling also showed slower n=2048. Expanding to batch=60,n=1024 validated but regressed more to 117509.878 us. Removing the orthogonality guard was invalid: differential guard caught an n=2048 dense seed with large R-Q.T@A residual. The compact-Householder conversion via geqrf(Q) appears to erase Cholesky-QR savings; next attempts need a direct Q/R-to-H,tau construction or a different true Householder panel/TSQR Triton path.

From e822fc30, add exact per-matrix tail-zero routing for mixed n=512/1024 batches: use Triton certification to produce a boolean mask, keep the existing whole-batch fast path when all matrices certify, otherwise compact certified matrices into leading-panel geqrf subbatches, zero-embed and scatter H,tau by original indices, and route uncertified or stride-ambiguous cases through full geqrf.

Added Triton per-matrix tail-zero certification for n=512/1024, preserving whole-batch fast path when all certify and otherwise compacting certified matrices into panel geqrf subbatches while full-geqrf routes uncertified matrices, then scattering H/tau back. Validation passed and benchmark improved to 113135.683 us.

Added a minimum certified-matrix threshold before mixed compact/scatter routing to avoid small subbatches. Validation passed but benchmark was slightly worse at 113167.213 us, so the prior always-route-certified approach remains better.

Continued from e822fc30 and implemented exact per-matrix tail-zero routing for n=512/1024. Triton now certifies a boolean mask per matrix; all-certified batches keep the whole-batch panel geqrf fast path, mixed batches compact certified matrices into a panel-geqrf subbatch, full-geqrf uncertified matrices, and scatter H/tau back by original indices. Validation and guards passed. Best benchmark was 113135.683 us at 47d4bdb0, improving baseline 115508.049 and parent. A minimum-certified threshold variant validated but was slightly worse at 113167.213 us, so it was logged and reset. Final profile captured for 47d4bdb0.

Starting from 47d4, reduce host sync and indexing overhead in exact per-matrix tail-zero routing for mixed n=512/1024 while keeping 47d4 certification and fallback decisions bit-for-bit identical; measure sync/index cost, then try GPU-resident fixed-mask scatter or prefix compaction only if it removes certified.sum().item()/nonzero CPU roundtrips without changing order or fallback coverage.

Tried eliminating certified.sum/nonzero CPU roundtrips for fixed benchmark batch shapes by computing both panel and full geqrf then GPU-selecting per matrix with torch.where. Validation passed but benchmark regressed badly to 162733.976 us because full geqrf still runs for all matrices plus extra panel/select work.

Added a cheap all-certified tail-zero precheck using the existing Triton single-flag scan before the per-matrix mask path. This preserves fallback decisions but avoids per-matrix mask/sum/nonzero overhead for whole-batch rankdef cases. Validation passed and benchmark improved to 112987.942 us.

Explored sync/index overhead reductions from 47d4 while preserving certification/fallback decisions. A GPU-resident mask-select variant removed CPU roundtrips but validated at 162733.976 us because it computed full geqrf for every matrix plus panel/select work, so it was logged and reset. The successful refinement adds a cheap all-certified Triton single-flag precheck before per-matrix mask/nonzero; this avoids per-matrix sync/index overhead on whole-batch rankdef cases and improved benchmark to 112987.942 us. Final commit 3f3a9a0e validated, benchmarked, and profiled.

Base on 3f3a9a0 and apply only f414 n=512 scan-block tuning by setting _has_tail_nonzero and _tail_zero_mask block choice to 4096 for n=512; preserve 3f3 all-certified precheck, per-matrix routing, fallback path, and all n=1024 behavior exactly, then validate and benchmark whether the scan tuning stacks.

Validation passed, but benchmark was 113144.076 us, worse than 3f3 parent 112987.942 us.
